articleTitle: Technical literature [Reprint of "Field-Effect Transistor Memory" (US Patent No. 3,387,286)]
abstract: Presents a reproduction of Robert H. Dennard's ground breaking patent for one-transistor dynamic random access memory (DRAM) that led to major increases in computer memory density and decreases in cost.

articleTitle: Microwatt Switched Capacitor Circuit Design, E. Vittoz, Presented at a Summer Course on Switched Capacitor Circuits, June 9–12, 1981, ESAT, KU Leuven
abstract: Exemplifying the contributions of Dr. Eric Vittoz to low-voltage, low-power CMOS logic, this paper examines the CMOS implementation of the three basic components of SC circuits in the context of low power and low voltage, and explores the trade-off between lower power, settling time, and noise considerations. This paper will be reprinted in full in the Fall 2008 SSCS News.

articleTitle: Timekeeper (U.S. Patent No. 3,895,486) W. Hammer, E. Vittoz, J. Hermann, H. Choffat, 1975
abstract: Patented in 1975, Eric Vittoz's "Timekeeper" was comprised of a quartz crystal resonator with a stable frequency and a relatively large tolerance, and a frequency divider with an adjustable division ratio. This divider had auxiliary electrical inputs whose logical state determined the division ratio, and an electrically alterable electronic memory that supplyied stored data to determine the logical state of the auxiliary inputs and the division ratio. The SSCS News provides pages 1-2 of this patent.

articleTitle: Complementary-MOS Low-Power Low-Voltage Integrated Binary Counter
abstract: In May 1962, Dr. Eric Vittoz was the first electrical engineer hired by Centre Electronique Horloger (CEH), the research laboratory founded in Neuchatel, Switzerland by several organizations representing most of the Swiss watch industry. This paper represents Dr. Vittoz's early work there on an integrated complementary MOS-transistor binary counter stage realized in monolithic form, which allowed p-channel and n-channel MOSTs to be grouped together within two distinct surface areas, resulting in a reduction of the surface necessary for given circuit functions. The integrated frequency divider was used in the first prototypes of electronic watches.

articleTitle: Frequency Divider Circuit (U.S. Patent No. 3,619,646) Eric Andre Vittoz, 1971
abstract: Granted in 1971, Eric Vittoz's patent for the first binary frequency divider was used in the first prototypes of the electronic watch. His frequency divider circuit included at least one logical structure complying with certain Boole Relations including two complementary input quantities and two output quantities. The logical structure comprised three pairs of field effect transistors, such as MOS-transistors having isolated gates. A cascade of such binary frequency divider circuits could be made as an integrated circuit. The SSCS News includes pages 1-2 of this patent.

articleTitle: Eric Vittoz and the Strong Impact of Weak Inversion Circuits
abstract: In a groundbreaking and now classic 1977 paper, Eric Vittoz and J. Fellrath meticulously characterized and developed models for devices operating in the weak inversion region, as well as a variety of circuit building blocks that could operate and exploit the exponential characteristics in this region. Their killer application -- the electronic watch -- employed techniques that are now used in a score of low-voltage, micropower applications, such as biomedical devices, hearing aids, pagers, sensor interfaces, motion detectors for pointing devices, and a variety of portable instruments. This tribute to Vittoz as an educator and industrial researcher is by Yannis Tsividis of Columbia University, an esteemed scientist and educator in his own right.

articleTitle: The Role of the Trench Capacitor in DRAM Innovation
abstract: Cost has been the strongest driving force for growing the DRAM market. Since die cost is closely related to the number of dies on a wafer, wafer diameter size has continually increased, and memory cell size has been reduced. To cope with the resulting dilemma of cell size vs. capacitance, the author invented the trench capacitor cell. The author documents its implementation, the "soft-error problem" that ensued, and efforts to solve it.

articleTitle: Turning students on to circuits
abstract: When one compares today's students to those of earlier generations, the differences are striking. Yet the way most of us teach has essentially remained unchanged since the middle of the past century. No wonder, then, that our students are not attracted to electrical engineering or, among those who are, many are disappointed and just drag along, or even drop out. In this article we discuss what can be done to turn things around. Parts of this article draw on an earlier one on an introductory EE class.

articleTitle: The Stacked Capacitor DRAM Cell and Three-Dimensional Memory
abstract: The author chronicles the development of the stacked three-dimensional (3D) DRAM cell, highlighting his role in solving the problems of memory data-bandwidth and forecasting a dramatic increase in memory capacity based on his current work using "super-chip" integration technology.

articleTitle: The History of DRAM Circuit Designs – At the Forefront of DRAM Development –
abstract: Dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) has been the only high-density RAM used for over 30 years despite many attempts to replace it. Contributing to IT advances to this day, it has achieved an unprecedented six-fold increase in memory capacity in the last three decades. The author surveys the history of DRAM circuit design in this paper, based on his career at the forefront of DRAM development from its inception in 1970 through the present.

articleTitle: Revisiting "Evolution of the MOSFET Dynamic RAM – A Personal View"
abstract: This first-person account of the early days of semiconductor memory development is reprinted from the IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices, Vol ED-31, no 11, Nov. 1984, pp 1549-1555. In it the author explains how his invention of DRAM came about and he chronicles the evolution of DRAM technology from 1967 through 1984. In that period, he reports, there was a lot of circuit and architectural innovation in a very competitive environment, with little documentation in the public literature.

articleTitle: A Returnee from the US Becomes Entrepreneur in China, Beken Corporation Founder Muses about the IC Community in Shanghai
abstract: Founder of Beken Corporation Muses about the IC Community in Shanghai As an entrepreneur returning to the land of my birth from the USA to found and lead one of the burgeoning IC design houses in China, I encountered challenges and difficulties and tastes of success, too, sometimes with a bit of luck. Deeply submerged in the world's largest consumer market, inside a fast-growing design community with intensive semiconductor supply chain contacts and an extremely active capital market, I plan to report my first hand observations in my column for readers of the IEEE SSCS News. So stay tuned to the east side of the globe!

articleTitle: The Remarkable Story of the DRAM Industry
abstract: Early in the development of computers, it was recognized that a hierarchy of memory was essential to enable timely access to data. Due to its relatively low cost and high access speed, Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) technology has had a virtual monopoly on the main memory segment. Dr. Randy Isaac examines some of the key factors that determined the success of the DRAM industry since its beginnings in 1970.

articleTitle: Executive Summary: Advances in Ultra-Low-Voltage Design
abstract: The idea of exploiting weak-inversion operation for low power circuits was pioneered by Dr. Eric Vittoz in the 1960's, and has led to many recent advances in sub-threshold circuit design. Today, sub-threshold operation provides a compelling solution for a number of emerging energy-constrained systems implemented in scaled CMOS technologies. This article by Joyce Kwong and Anantha Chandrakasan, to be printed in full in the SSCS Fall News, outlines some recent advances and challenges associated with sub-threshold circuit design, including the design of new logic and memory circuits, support circuitry, and the use of redundancy.

articleTitle: Introduction to “In Quest of the Joy of Creation”
abstract: New introductory remarks introduce a reprint of the authors' 2005 article "In Quest of the Joy of Creation." The original article is reproduced from "Innovate the Future," 2005 Hitachi Hyoron Special Edition, pp. 34-39, Hitachi Hyoronsha, Tokyo, Japan. In it the author recalls his 42-year career at Hitachi, focusing on DRAM design there since the early 1970s. Entrusted with developing a 4-Kb DRAM at the the outset of his career and without any knowledge of semiconductors, the author became the lead designer of the first prototype for each of eight successive generations of Hitachi DRAMs. Faced with the challenge of breaking through limits on each consecutive generation, and after failing four times, Hitachi finally won the race with its 64-Kb DRAM.

articleTitle: TOOLS: How to Write Readable Reports and Winning Proposals Part 5: Persuasive External Proposals
abstract: Part 5: Persuasive External Proposals Two keys to a winning proposal are 1] an executive summary that states the benefits of your solution and ties them to customer needs and 2] detail that backs it up crisply and without techno-babble.

articleTitle: Symbiosis in the Technology World
abstract: The trick in any symbiotic arrangement is to bind it with deliverables that can and act as a convenient brake if the project starts to go off the rails and enable you to track and measure output to justify your resource expenditure and facilitate staged payment deals. A workable relationship depends upon the parties involved and the nature of the programme. In some cases, its value may lie in the unbounded, free thinking that academics can bring to the dynamics. In other cases, closely confined, structured research may be more applicable to realize the aspirations of the commercial partners. Either way, whatever is decided needs to be agreed upfront and be manageable. Intellectual property issues, such as sole right to use versus open access, single versus multiple use licences, royalty based agreements based upon volume sales, one-off costs and inferred rights transfer, indemnification and post sales support, can run aground for a variety of reasons. My advice is simple -- be realistic.

articleTitle: Tools: Tips for Making Writing Easier, Part 1: The Five-Minute Miracle
abstract: Just imagine a reader saying "I have only one minute. What do you want to tell me?" Then set your timer for five minutes. Use the first to state your main message. Then invite your 'reader' to ask you two critical questions to clarify it. After writing your main message and preparing answers to his or her most pressing questions, you will have a solid, short missive only a few sentences long. "The Five- Minute Miracle" will work for an e-mail, a short report, an executive summary, or a short introductory proposal.

articleTitle: Executive Summary: Gigasensors for an Attoscope
abstract: The introduction of silicon chips in particle physics experiments went by steps. In this summary of an article to be printed in full in the Fall News, Erik Heijne of CERN, the elementary particle accelerator laboratory in Geneva, Switzerland, traces some of the history of silicon detectors and readout chips for tracking detectors that form the inner shells of the equipment.

articleTitle: Kuroda Speaks in Seoul on CMOS Proximity Inter-Chip Communications
abstract: SSCS Distinguished Lecturer Tadahiro Kuroda of Keio University presented a talk to an appreciative audience of 120 at Ewha Womans University on 15 November, 2007. According to Seoul Chapter member Sung Min Park, most faculty members at the lecture work in related areas; many undergraduate student attendeess were familiar with Dr. Kuroda's subject from a course on microelectronics.

articleTitle: History of the Development of Swiss Watch Microprocessors
abstract: While the microprocessors used today in most personal computers, PDA's and self-phones are very well known, the evolution of watch microprocessors is a completely unknown and a very "Swiss" or "Neuchatel" story. Christian Piguet, a designer of low-power low-voltage integrated circuits in CMOS technology and the author of more than a dozen patents on digital design, microprocessors and watch systems, provides a first hand view of this chronology.

articleTitle: Microwatt Switched Capacitor Circuit Design: Prepared for a Summer Course at K.U. Leuven, 1981
abstract: Summer Course on Switched Capacitor Circuits, June 9-12, 1981, K. U. Leuven Eric Vittoz prepared this seminal paper in 1981 for a summer course at K.U.Leuven. After reviewing the behavior of MOS devices at very low current, it examines the CMOS implementation of the three basic components of SC circuits (switches, matched capacitors, amplifiers), and weighs the tradeoffs between low power, settling time, and noise considerations.

articleTitle: Tools: Tips for Making Writing Easier, Part 2: Narrow Your Questions, Shape Your Answers
abstract: Part 2: Narrow Your Questions, Shape Your Answers In "The Five-Minute Miracle" -- a quick and easy way to approach a short piece of writing (reprinted in the Spring '08 SSCS News) -- you set up an imaginary conversation with your reader, beginning with your main message and continuing with answers that anticipate his or her probable questions about that message. Using the "Key Point & Backup" method, you give each answer first and then make that answer credible by bolstering it with an example, illustration, or explanation.

articleTitle: Tools: Tips for Making Writing Easier, Part 3: Focus on Your Key Message
abstract: Part 3: Focus on Your Key Message To focus your message on what you are trying to say, put your main thought in the main parts of the sentence: the subject, verb, and object. Say your sentences to yourself before you write them down. Choose the best words and place them in the most readable order, with key words at the end of each sentence, where they get the most emphasis. Yogi Berra is famous for saying "When you come to a fork in the road, take it" (not "Take a fork in the road when you come to it.") Don't just trust your voice -- use it.

articleTitle: Bell's Law for the Birth and Death of Computer Classes: A theory of the Computer's Evolution
abstract: In 1951 a man could walk inside a computer. By 2010, a computer cluster with millions of processors will have expanded to building size. In this new paper Gordon Bell explains the history of the computing industry, positing a general theory ("Bell's Law) for the creation, evolution, and death of computer classes since 1951. Using the exponential transistor density increases forecast by Moore's Law in 1965 and 1975 as the principal basis for the life cycle of computer classes after the microprocessor was introduced in 1971, he predicts that the powerful microprocessor will be the basis for nearly all computer classes in 2010, from personal computers and servers costing a few thousand dollars to scalable servers costing a few hundred million dollars. Soon afterward, billions of cell phones for personal computing, and tens of billions of wireless sensor nets will unwire and interconnect everything.

articleTitle: A Short Story of the EKV MOS Transistor Model
abstract: The EKV MOS transistor model and design methodology evolved from the first weak inversion transistor models of the 1970's. In this first-hand account, Christian Enz chronicles the evolution of the hierarchical structure, limited parameters and flexibility of the EKV model that he developed with colleagues such as Francois Krummenacher and Eric Vittoz (the "E" "K" and "V" of EKV) at the Centre Electronique Horloger (CEH) in Neuchatel. With the aggressive downscaling of CMOS technologies today, the EKV compact model is shifting increasingly from the traditional strong inversion region toward moderate and weak inversion regions.

articleTitle: The Electronic Watch and Low-Power Circuits
abstract: Renowned as an expert in low-power CMOS circuit design and for groundbreaking work with miniature electronic devices, Dr. Eric A. Vittoz relates his life, work and times in this original retrospective for the SSCS News. According to Yannis Tsividis, also in this issue, Dr. Vittoz's influence continues to grow, as low voltage and low power become increasingly important in the engineering of mobile devices. Dr. Vittoz is a Research Fellow at the Swiss Center for Electronics and Microtechnology in Neuchatel, Switzerland, an IEEE Fellow, and a professor at EPFL, the Ecole Polytechnique Federale de Lausanne. He has published more than 130 papers and holds 26 patents.

articleTitle: Advances in Ultra-Low-Voltage Design
abstract: The idea of exploiting weak-inversion operation for low power, pioneered by Dr. Eric Vittoz in the 1960's, has led to many recent advances in sub-threshold circuit design, described in this paper by MIT's Anantha Chandrakasan and Joyce Kwong. In the near future, exciting new applications such as medical monitoring, toxic gas sensors and next-generation portable video gadgets in a number of systems will be powered by energy scavenging technologies that will require electronic circuits to operate with the utmost energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Gigasensors for an Attoscope: Catching Quanta in CMOS
abstract: Around 1987, Eric Vittoz studied the basic parameters for the development of 'pixel' particle tracking detectors in collaboration with a team in Geneva at CERN. CERN scientist Erik Heijne traces the evolution of these particle imagers, which has resulted in matrices of 256x256 pixels with > 1000 transistors per pixel that can process single quanta and have connections with neighboring cells allowing analog and logic operations at ns time-scale for distributed events.

articleTitle: It's about Time: A Brief Chronology of Chronometry
abstract: The evolution of clock making, recounted in this article by Thomas H. Lee, advanced dramatically after low-power, quartz-controlled watches were first developed by Eric Vittoz and others at the Centre Electronique Horloger (CEH) over forty years ago. Due in great part to their work, even the least expensive wristwatches today are so precise that the need for better stability no longer drives their evolution. Instead, the ability to integrate more functions per unit volume explains why many watches are becoming multipurpose information appliances including PDAs, infrared remote controls, pagers, radios, TVs, walkie-talkies and MP3 players. In the future, low-power will become increasingly important as engineers struggle to address the constrained power budgets of the wristwatch form factor.

articleTitle: DRAM – A Personal View
abstract: Based on his work in the design, specification and test of DRAM for over thirty years, Dr. Richard Foss charts the crucial role of Dynamic Random Access Memory in the intertwined development of the computer and semiconductor industries, and highlights the influence of Moore's Law, whose tentacles reach into every aspect of modern life.

articleTitle: What should an Educated Person Know About Computers?
abstract: Everyone has high speed Internet access, everyone uses email to keep in touch with friends and family, and we all shop and search online. But most of the computing iceberg lies hidden below the surface. My view of what an educated person should know about computing focuses on three core pieces: hardware, software, and communications.

articleTitle: Watch microelectronics: Pioneer in portable consumer electronics
abstract: Mougahed Darwish, Marc Degrauwe, Thomas E. Gyger, Gunther Meusburger and Jean Claude Robert - a group of Swiss engineers at ETA and EM Microelectronic, the semiconductor manufacturer of the Swatch Group - describe the consraints of the watch-making industry that have shaped watch microelectronics, and relate how the pioneering skills and solutions of quartz watch-making have diffused into other portable consumer electronics applications.

articleTitle: ISSCC Replay on Demand, Too Tight a Personal Schedule?, Recalcitrant Management?, So you missed ISSCC this year!
abstract: Now ISSCC offers the second best thing to being there: All regular papers from the 2008 Conference recorded, with visuals, cursor overlay and movement, and speaker audio, available in June of this year. The 2008 version includes access to similar recordings from ISSCC 2007. You may purchase your personal subscription at www.isscc.org for $200.

articleTitle: Seeking Nominations for IEEE Medals and Recognitions
abstract: The IEEE Awards Board is seeking nominations for IEEE Medals and Recognitions. The Potential Nominee Form is available on the IEEE Awards Web Page at www.ieee.org/portal/pages/about/awards/noms/potnomform.html. The deadline for submitting an official nomination form for any IEEE medal or recognition is 1 July 2008.

articleTitle: SSCS Far East Chapters Meet in Jeju, Korea on 13 November, 2007
abstract: Coinciding with the 3rd annual A-SSCC, the 2nd SSCS Region 10 chapter meeting was chaired by Jan Van der Spiegel and attended by AdCom President-Elect Willy Sansen, SSCS Region 10 Representative C.K. Wang, and the officers of eight local Chapters.

articleTitle: F. Svelto Presents Short Course on CMOS Wireless Receiver Design in Hsinchu and Taipei, IEEE SSCS Taipei Chapter
abstract: Wireless Receiver Architectures and Front-end Design in CMOS' offered an introduction to several popular receiver architectures and key performance parameters for wireless receivers, plus a detailed explanation of the design principles of two important receiver front-end circuits: low-noise amplifier (LNA) and mixer. A second-day session on circuit design focused on techniques that realize high IIP2 mixers and multi-band LNA design and its application to multi-standard receiver systems. Approximately 75 participants attended the short course, which was underwritten by the SSCS Chapter Extra Subsidy Program.

articleTitle: SSCS-Scotland Sponsors Technical Meeting in September, K. Kundert Speaks on Verification of Complex Analog Circuits
abstract: K. Kundert Speaks on Verification of Complex Analog Circuits Around 40 people from local industry and academia gathered at the Central Edinburgh offices of Dialog Semiconductor on 28 September, 2008 to hear Dr. Ken Kundert, creator of "The Designer's Guide Community" website, talk about Verification of Complex Analog Integrated Circuits. The event was sponsored by the SSCS-Scotland chapter.

articleTitle: President's Message
abstract: It is with great pleasure and a sense of duty, that I have taken up the position of President of the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Society. I want to thank Dick Jaeger for his guidance and wise suggestions during the preceding years; I know I will be able to count on him, and I appreciate it. The Society is most famous for its Journal of Solid-Sate Circuits and its conferences, all of which will have to be rethought to find an answer to the surge in multimedia tools. Virtual journals, virtual conferences, and Xplore are being discussed on various levels; actions have already been taken and will be followed up. Recent AdCom Chair appointments are Bill Bidermann for the Meetings Committee and Glenn Gulak for the Publications Committee, with Bram Nauta as General Editor of the Journal. This is a new team indeed. I am looking forward to working with all of them towards a better SSCS.

articleTitle: Lanzerotti Applauded for Editorship of LEOS Newsletter
abstract: Mary Lanzerotti was presented with the IEEE/LEOS 2007 Distinguished Service Award for dedicated service as Editor of the LEOS Newsletter from 2001 through 2006 by Alan Willner, LEOS President in a ceremony during the Society's Awards Banquet on 23 October in Lake Buena Vista, Florida.

articleTitle: Congratulations new Senior Members
abstract: A list of 20 newly elected IEEE Senior Members is presented. They were Elected in August and September and are: B. Bakkaloglu, D. Blaauw, O. Buhler, D. Chiang, C. Debono, M. Fischer, K. articleTitle: Betty Prince Talks in Brazil
abstract: SSCS DL Betty Prince presented the plenary address and a tutorial at the Congresso Chip in Rio Conference on 5 September, 2007 in Rio de Janiero.

articleTitle: Process to Become a Petition Candidate for AdCom
abstract: Call for Nominations for Sensors Awards, Deadline for three awards is August 15

articleTitle: President's Message
abstract: SSCS members ask me, is hardware disappearing? Has it gone virtual, or has it been globalized out? The Journal of Solid-State Circuits is hardware. However, the thick pack of paper we are used to receiving every month is disappearing, virtualized together, perhaps, with our desk. Nowadays the circuit "paper" comes in layers, organized per screen. The layers go up and down -- up for the applications, down for the circuit details -- with one delta of understanding added per screen. Thus, design has gone virtual. Or is it the hardware (chip) that has gone virtual? Has the design of this hardware gone soft? A conference, on the other hand, is like the premiere of a painting exhibit. We receive a catalogue beforehand. Then we then get together with a few colleagues or friends to make a short tour. We exchange our impressions and at the reception at the end we have a drink (free for SSCS members).

articleTitle: Dennard Receives Medal from Benjamin Franklin Institute
abstract: Dr. Robert Dennard was honored in a dinner ceremony at Philadelphia's Benjamin Franklin Institute on 27 April 2007 by Dr. Peter J. Collings, Past Chairman of the Institute's Committee on Science and the Arts, and Dr. Dennis M. Wint, President and CEO, for "inventing the 1-transistor/1-capacitor Dynamic Random Access Memory that significantly reduced the cost of memory, and for contributing to the development of the metal oxide semiconductor scaling principle that guides the design of increasingly small and complex integrated circuits."

articleTitle: President's Message
abstract: Richard C. Jaeger's term as President saw SSCS conferences attracting record numbers of papers and attendees, the Journal of Solid-State Circuits continuing to have high download rates, and chapter activities and financial reserves at record levels. As of January 1, 2008, Willy Sansen, Professor at KU Leuven, Belgium and Director of ESAT-MICAS, became President. Well known internationally for his work in analog circuits, Dr. Sansen has been involved in a wide range of IEEE activities including Society Vice President and Chair of the 2002 ISSCC.

articleTitle: SSCS-Seoul Chapter was Local Organizing Committee for A-SSCC 2007
abstract: IEEE SSCS/EDS Seoul hosted the third Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference (A-SSCC 2007) on 12-14 November on the beautiful island seashore of Jeju, Korea. In order to provide unique opportunities for design experts and leaders in technology and business to gather in Asia, the conference takes place each year in a region with rapidly growing IC research, production and sales. It convened in Taiwan in 2005, China in 2006, and Korea in 2007.

articleTitle: Congratulations New Senior Members, 20 Seniors Elected in May, June and July and August
abstract: A list of 20 newly elected IEEE Senior Members is presented. The Society wishes to congratulate: D. Brookshire, D. Calbaza, J. Chu, F. Dunlap, L.F. Neto, P.Francis, K. Ghadiri, S. abstract: On page 5 of the SSCS News Vol. 13, No.2, the author of "Charles Babbage and the Quest to Build the First Computer," should be Swade, not "Swore."

articleTitle: Letters to the Editor
abstract: Thomas Lee's "Tales of the Continuum: A Subsampled History of Analog Circuits" ( Fall 2007) should have referenced the op amp of Karl D. Swartzel, Jr., who was Bell Labs' designer of the original amplifier used in the M-9 analog computational system (US patent 2401779).

articleTitle: SSCS-Singapore Hosts 90 at ISSCC 2007 Tutorial in August, DVD Replay Combined with Colloquium on How to Write an ISSCC Paper
abstract: Replay Combined with Colloquium on How to Write an ISSCC Paper To encourage submissions to ISSCC from industry in Asia, SSCS-Singapore hosted an ISSCC 2009 promotional event in August featuring a replay of the 2007 Conference tutorial "Continuous-time Sigma-Delta Data Converters" at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering of the National University of Singapore. The event was free of charge and open to academics, students, and engineers from local industry.

articleTitle: SSCS DL Stefan Rusu Speaks at Santa Clara Valley Chapter Meeting in August
abstract: SSCS DL Stefan Rusu, a Senior Principal Engineer at Intel Corporation, addressed the Society's Santa Clara Valley chapter on 21 August about "Power and Leakage Reduction in the Nanoscale Era." Lectures by Ali Niknejad of UC Berkeley, Michael H. Perrott of MIT, and Boris Murmann of Stanford are planned for the chapter's September, October and November meetings, respectively.

articleTitle: Call for Nominations: SSCS Predoctoral Fellowships 2008 – 2009, Due Date is 1 May, 2008
abstract: Due Date is 1 May, 2008 . Nominations for the Society's Predoctoral Fellowships in solid-state circuits are due on 1 May, 2008 for the academic year 2008-2009. The one-year awards will provide $15,000 for tuition, up to $8000 in addition for fees, and a grant of $2,000 to the department in which the recipient is registered. A maximum of two awards will be made. Last year's predoctoral fellows were Jintae Kim of UCLA and Sudip Shekhar of the University of Washington.

articleTitle: Call for Fellow Nominations
abstract: Nominations are being accepted until March 1, 2008 for the 2009 class of IEEE Fellows. To encourage more Fellow nominations from industry, nominees are now classified as Research Engineer/Scientist, Application Engineer/Practitioner, Technical Leader, or Educator.

articleTitle: Introduction
abstract: According to Dr. Erik H. M. Heijne, who originated the concept of the Summer '08 issue, the reciprocity between microelectronics and consumer products and habits is perfectly illustrated by the summer 2008 issue of the SSCS News in first-hand accounts that reveal how the use of microelectronics circuits in wristwatches has forced them to improve power usage and tools for device and circuit simulation. This collection demonstrates the dynamic of IEEE as an international community of engineers with high profile and great potential, and will assuredly lead to new ideas and stimulate many in our community

articleTitle: Congratulations New Senior Members, 24 Elected in October and December 2007
abstract: 24 Elected in October and December 2007 Rui Aguiar, Thomas Amberg, Mel Bazes, Peter Beerel, Marc Belleville, Didier Belot, Yut Chow, Jan Craninckx, John Ebner, Hans Eichel, Dennis Ferguson, Richard Ferrant, Patrick Garda, Andrea Gerosa, David Gulbransen, Suhwan Kim, Guido Masera, Ian O'Connor, Richard Perdriau, Moises Robinson, Zhenhua Shao, W Sung, Chih-Kong Yang, Alireza Zolfaghari.

articleTitle: President's Message
abstract: At its August meeting, the SSCS AdCom celebrated the conversion of the Society's Newsletter into a Magazine and heard a breathtaking preview of how ISSCC might look in 2020. According to conference spokesman Dennis Monticelli, the ISSCC may go virtual, with e-papers, an e-digest, and other complementary materials such as an e-journal developed as a result. Task Force actions taken to date will result in four experimental satellite conferences next year in the Far East, within three weeks of the ISSCC. This project not only addresses the future of the ISSCC, but of all SSCS conferences, even conferences in general.

articleTitle: 2007 Update DVD Needs Foundations Disk, Reminder for SSCS Members who Attended ISSCC 2008
abstract: Reminder for SSCS Members Who Attended ISSCC 2008 Are you an SSCS member who picked up the Society Archive DVD Update for 2007 included in your registration at February's ISSCC? If you need a Foundation disk, please send an email requesting it to Katherine Olstein (k.olstein@ieee.org) with your member number and complete postal address. The Foundation Disks will be mailed to requesters in May.

articleTitle: Clark Nguyen Presents DL Talk on RF-MEMS in Japan
abstract: SSCS Distinguished Lecturer Clark T.-C. Nguyen presented a talk entitled "Integrated Micromechanical Circuits for RF Front-Ends" to a crowd of 150 at Nihon Dempa Kogyo (NDK) in Sayama-city, Saitama, Japan on 24 April, 2008. The one and one-half hour lecture and discussion was part of NDK's annual engineer educational program. Dr. Nguyen gave a shorter version of this talk at the 2008 IEEE VLSI-TSA plenary session in Taiwan and presented another DL talk on behalf of the Society at National Semiconductor in Santa Clara, CA on 8 May.

articleTitle: ISSCC Student Forum
abstract: Thirty graduate students from around the world met in February 2008 preceding the ISSCC to exchange brief presentations about their work in progress. According to Patrick Mercier, a graduate student from MIT, "the short five minute presentations encouraged students to succinctly present only their key ideas and contributions - a skill that is becoming increasingly important today's busy world." A Call for Participation in the 2009 Student Forum will be available in November at www.isscc.org.

articleTitle: CEDA Celebrates Second Anniversary
abstract: Since its inception, CEDA has taken the leadership in cosponsoring DAC, ICCAD, and DATE, and now sponsors 12 conferences and workshops focusing on specific topics or regions. Recently, the Test Technology Technical Council (TTTC) joined CEDA and the IEEE Computer Society Press in publishing the IEEE D&T Electronic Edition. A hardware-software codesign contest to identify issues in codesign practice and to foster greater interest in the design aspects of MEMOCODE began this year at the The 5th ACM/IEEE International MEMCODE conference in Nice.

articleTitle: Santa Clara Valley Chapter Sponsors RFIC Course
abstract: Rights and PermissionsA successful RFIC Design Course on two consecutive weekdays, from October 15 - 16, 2007 attracted over 70 participants. The six 50-minute lectures and two major addresses featured Allen Podell, J.L. Julian Tham, Thomas Lee, Dr. Derek Shaeffer, Dr. Masoud Zargari, Dr. Alon Konchitsky, Dr. Narendra Rao, and Dr. Alireza Shirvani

articleTitle: First IEEE COMCAS a Mega Event in Tel Aviv, SSC Sessions Span two Days
abstract: SSC Sessions Span Two Days Building on the yearly IEEE Israel AP/MTT & AES Chapters Symposium, COMCAS 2008, an exciting two-day conference and exposition, was a multidisciplinary forum for internationally recognized scientists and engineers and students, with over 700 participants, 146 papers, 15 technical sessions, five parallel meeting rooms, a large professional exhibition with 62 booths, and an impressive list of speakers, including expert R&D engineers, top scientists and managers from Asia, the US, Europe, Latin America, the Far East and Israel.

articleTitle: 21 SSCS Chapters Represented at February Meeting in San Francisco
abstract: Representatives from thirteen SSCS chapters in the Americas and Canada, and nine from Europe and the Far East, attended the Society's annual Chapter Chair Luncheon and Meeting on 5 February 2008. The AdCom presented Chapters Chair Jan Van der Spiegel with a special award of recognition for his stewardship of the program for the past 11 years. SSCS Region 10 Representative C. K. Wang delivered the Chapter Committee's certificate of appreciation to Shen-Iuan Liu, past Chair of SSCS-Taipei, "in recognition and appreciation of his outstanding service as Chair of the Taipei Chapter of the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Society 2005-2008."

articleTitle: SSCS-Taipei Offers Short Course on CMOS Single-Chip Radio Design, Programs in Hsinchu and Taipei Funded by SSCS Extra Chapter Subsidy
abstract: Programs in Hsinchu and Taipei Funded by SSCS Extra Chapter Subsidy Approximately 80 participants attended a two-day course sponsored by SSCS-Taipei at National Chiao-Tung University in Hsinchu and at National Taiwan University, Taipei on August 20 and 21, 2008, respectively. The presentations by Dr. Bogdan Staszewski of Texas Instruments entitled "Digital RF Processor (DRPTM) for Single-chip Mobile Radios: All-digital PLL, Transmitter and Discrete-time Receiver" were made possible by an SSCS chapter subsidy.   lost this piece, recaptureonline

articleTitle: AdCom Endorses Newsletter Conversion to Magazine, Supports Chandrakasan as ISSCC Conference Chair in 2010
abstract: Supports Chandrakasan as ISSCC Conference Chair in 2010 . The AdCom voted to proceed with Phase I of the IEEE process to convert the SSCS Newsletter into a magazine. The final decision of the Technical Activities Board (TAB) will be made in June and publicized during the fall member renewal period. As a publication available in IEEE Xplore, the Solid-State Circuits Magazine will more effectively reach the worldwide IC community and attract top-ranking contributors. The AdCom also appropriated $100K for ISSCC's Virtual Conference project for posting conference sessions on-line. In additional motions, it endorsed the contiuation of a member development initiative in the Far East and the new, Saturday evening student session at ISSCC.

articleTitle: R. Jacob Baker Honored at FIE Conference in October
abstract: Dr. R. Jacob Baker was presented with the Hewlett-Packard Frederick Emmons Terman Award on 14 October, 2007 at the meeting of the Frontiers in Education Conference in Milwaukee as "an outstanding young electrical engineering educator in recognition of his contribution to the profession."

articleTitle: Oregon State University Student Branch Chapter Inaugurated in March, Prof. Tom Lee Presents a History of Radio
abstract: As its inaugural activity, the Oregon State University (OSU) SSCS Student Branch Chapter hosted a presentation by SSCS distinguished lecturer Tom H. Lee on the history of radio. The OSU SSCS student chapter was founded in 2007 to help students interact and communicate with experts and to promote membership in SSCS by demonstrating what we do and what we intend to do through the Engineering Expo at OSU and other local activities.

articleTitle: CEDA currents: IEEE/ACM MEMOCODE Contest Update
abstract: CEDA hosted a luncheon in June at this year's DAC to honor Robert Brayton, winner of the 2007 Phil Kaufman Award, for his impact on the field of electronic design through contributions in EDA. The eleven winning teams from the IEEE/ACMMEMOCODE Hardware/Software Codesign Contest in March were also formally announced.

articleTitle: Editor's Column
abstract: In this issue, Prof. Brian Kernighan has graciously agreed to write "What Should an Educated Person Know About Computers?" We are grateful that he has contributed this overview for SSCS News. We are delighted to report that Dr. Rakesh Kumar has agreed to join the editorial staff as Tutorials Editor, and Prof. Richard Jaeger will become Technical Editor. We are also happy to report that Katherine Olstein has joined the editorial staff as News Editor. Please do consider communicating information about news in your area to Katherine: k.olstein@ieee.org.

articleTitle: Eight Candidates Vie for Five AdCom Positions
abstract: The SSCS Administrative Committee will hold elections next fall. Tohru Furuyama, Bruce Gieseke, and Ken O are new candidates. Ali Hajimiri, Paul Hurst, and Ian Young are incumbents. C.-K. Wang, and Domine Leenaerts currently serve as appointed members of the AdCom and are running for election. A petition process is available for adding candidates.

articleTitle: Editor's Column
abstract: In Summer 2008, we feature the work and impact of Dr. Eric Vittoz, including an exclusive lead article by him entitled "Electronic Watch and Low Power Circuits." I am grateful to Dr. Erik Heijne for suggesting Dr. Vittoz as a potential subject and feature author, and for recommendating experts to attest to the impact of Dr. Vittoz's career on the development and commercialization of electronic Swiss watches. As a result, we are honored to offer original papers by Christian Enz, Thomas E. Gyger, et al., Tom Lee, Christian Piguet, and Yannis Tsividis. Two more papers by Eric Heijne and Joyce Kwong and Anantha Chandrakasan will appear in full in our Fall issue

articleTitle: Romania SSCS Chapter Formed to Promote Circuit Activities in Eastern Europe
abstract: SSCS-Romania, newly established last fall by Marcel Profirescu to foster a stronger connection between local academic and industrial circuit design researchers and the Romanian chapter of EDS, cosponsored a mini-colloquium with 15 well known international speakers as its first event. SSCS AdCom Endorses Newsletter-Magazine Conversion ISSCC Task Force Previews Ground-Breaking Initiatives In a formal motion at its biannual meeting on 19 August, 2008 in San Francisco, the SSCS AdCom endorsed the tone, scope, administrative structure, and budget of the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Magazine approved by the IEEE Technical Activities Board (TAB) in June. The Magazine will launch in January 2009 as an official migration of the SSCS Newsletter, which had become a magazine. The AdCom also heard about work in progress report on ISSCC spin-off "satellite" conferences and the ground-breaking technologies that will be necessary to support them.

articleTitle: Eight Society Members Congratulated at ISSCC for Elevation to IEEE Fellow Grade
abstract: During the ISSCC awards program, President Willy Sansen congratulated Kenji Anami, Patrick Gelsinger, Rakesh Kumar, Bram Nauta, Jyuo-Min Shyu, Stewart Taylor, C. K. Wang, and Hoi-Jun Yoo on their selection for the IEEE Fellow Class of 2008. A total of 295 IEEE Senior Members were elevated to Fellow Grade effective 1 January 2008.

articleTitle: Best Student Designs Spark Discussions at ISSCC 2008 Poster Sessions
abstract: Representatives of the nine projects winning the latest DAC-ISSCC student design contest, and members of the three top A-SSCC 2007 student design teams, drew crowds eager to discuss their work in evening poster sessions on 4- 5 February at ISSCC in San Francisco.

articleTitle: Mm-wave CMOS Applications: A Report from a CSICS Panel
abstract: Questions from experts at a panel discussion during the Compound Semi-Conductor IC Symposium in Portland Oregon on 29 November, 2007 focused on the prognosis for future applications and the feasibility of 60 GHz WLAN/WPAN in CMOS. The last question, contrasting optimal designs with business reality, posed W band as a solution having less path loss and greater bandwidth than 60 Hz. Answer: There are no standards being written for W band.

articleTitle: Murmann and Razavi Visit SSCS-Taipei
abstract: SSCS Extra Chapter Subsidy Underwrites Short Course on A/D Converter Design Boris Murmann of Stanford University presented a short course on deep-submicron ADC in Hsinchu and Taipei on 5-6 September, attracting over one hundred attendees from industry and academia. Two weeks later, SSCS DL Behzad Razavi of UCLA presented an invited talk on millimeter-wave circuit design at National Taiwan University (NTU).

articleTitle: Sakurai and Razavi Visit SSCS-Seoul in July and August
abstract: SSCS DL Takayasu Sakurai of Tokyo University spoke on "Organic Integrated Circuit Design for Ubiquitous Electronics" at Ewha Womans University on 6 July, 2007. Prof. Behzad Razavi presented a lecture entitled "60-GHz Transceivers in CMOS : Why and How?" on 14 August at Korea University, which houses a center for 60GHz wireless transceivers.

articleTitle: Ian Galton Speaks on “Performance Enhancement Techniques for Fractional-N PLLs” at SSCS-CASS/Atlanta
abstract: Nearly fifty attendees heard DL Ian Galton speak on PLLs at SSCS-Atlanta on 7 November, 2007. According to chapter member Oscar Palomino, "PLL technology is a very popular topic at Georgia Tech, which offers graduate courses and features various research teams developing novel designs on the subject."

articleTitle: Editor's column
abstract: The theme of this issue is "The DRAM Story," featuring reflections by Robert Dennard, Kiyoo Itoh, Hideo Sunami, Mitsumasa Koyanagi, Randy Isaac and Richard Foss on the evolution and current status of DRAM, as well as a feature article by Yannis Tsividis of Columbia University on on reforming EE undergraduate education.

articleTitle: Family Expectations Spawn Successful Careers, Arati Prabhakar Keynotes 2nd ISSCC Luncheon for Women in Solid-State Circuits
abstract: Arati Prabhakar Keynotes 2nd ISSCC Luncheon For Women In Solid-State Circuits The personal comments and outstanding credentials of Arati Prabhakar, a General Partner at US Venture Partners in Menlo Park, CA, held audience attention on 5 February, 2008 at the ISSCC Luncheon for Women in Solid-State Circuits. The ISSCC-sponsored luncheon for women in solid-state circuits aims to create a community for career support and a network for expanding the employment of women and minorities in industry.

articleTitle: Ankush Goel and Shih-An Yu Receive SSCS Predoctoral Fellowships for 2008–2009
abstract: According to SSCS reviewers, SSCS Predoctoral Fellowship Award winners Ankush Goel of USC and Shih-An Yu of Columbia University, "stand out through their excellent academic records and an impressive list of high-quality journal and conference publications." Their research "is very innovative and has the potential to have significant impact on the field of solid-state circuits."

articleTitle: Academia and Industry Interact in Ireland
abstract: SSCS DLs Pelgrom, Galton, and Castello Speak at Chapter Meetings To promote interaction between academia and the circuit design industry, SSCS-Ireland organized guest lectures this year by Marcel Pelgrom in Dublin, Ian Galton in Cork, and Rinaldo Castello, who spoke in Cork and in Limerick at the IEEJ Analog VLSI workshop.

articleTitle: Eight Technical Meetings in Fort Collins During 2007
abstract: SSCS DLs Fischette, Allstot and Nguyen Speak SSCS-Denver hosted eight seminars in 2007, including three sponsored by the Society's Distinguished Lecturer Series. The topics, spanning cutting-edge microprocessors, design techniques for high-speed serial links, and forefront technologies such as next-generation lithography were presented by SSCS DLs Dennis Fischette, David Allstot and Clark Nguyen and by Robin Porter, Troy Beukema, Shawn Searles, Gu-Yeon Wei and David Brooks, and Hugh Grinolds.

articleTitle: Fiez, Kuroda, Nauta, Sevenhans and Soyuer Elected to AdCom
abstract: Representing industry and academia, Asia, Europe, and North America, Terri Fiez, Tadahiro Kuroda, Bram Nauta, Jan Sevenhans and Mehmet Soyuer will serve on the SSCS AdCom for three year terms, from 1 January, 2008 through 31 December, 2010.

articleTitle: 3rd Annual Austin Conference on Integrated Systems & Circuits (ACISC), Meeting in ‟The Silicon Hills of the USA„ on May 7–9, 2008
abstract: Meeting in the "Silicon Hills of the USA" on 7-9 May, 2008   To be held this spring at the UT-Austin Commons Conference Center located on the J.J. Jake Pickle Research Campus of The University of Texas at Austin, ACISC serves as a local forum for the dissemination of technical information and advances in electronic technology at chip, board and system levels, covering design, CAD methodology, and testing.

articleTitle: SSCS-Israel Revitalized in Collaboration with IEEE MTT and AP Societies, Joint Conference on Microwave, Communication, Antenna and Electronic Systems (COMCAS) Will Debut in May
abstract: Joint Conference on Microwave, Communication, Antenna and Electronic Systems (COMCAS) Will Debut in May   Due to the many large multinationals with R&D centers in Israel like Intel, Freescale, Motorola, and IBM, and the large number of startups and fabless design centers, a lot of work in solid-state circuits is going on in Israel. COMCAS 2008 will bring engineers from many different technical areas together in one venue and capitalize on the cooperation of six local IEEE societies to organize a world-class, mega-event in Tel Aviv in May. The conference will be "international," with the official language being English.

articleTitle: SSCS-West Ukraine Joint Chapter: A Twelve Year Retrospective, IEEE Pioneer in Eastern Europe with MTT, ED, AP and CPMT
abstract: One of the first five chapters in Eastern Europe, and the first IEEE chapter in the Ukraine, SSCS-West Ukraine focuses on co-operation with the IEEE NULP and EDS Student branch chapters. Bimonthly technical meetings, social events, and major scientific conferences - notably DIPED, TCSET, YSC, and MEMSTEC - are organized by this community.

articleTitle: SSCS-Seoul Hosts DVD Replay of ISSCC, 2007 Short Courses, Celebrates 10th Chapter Anniversary
abstract: Celebrates 10th Chapter Anniversary   More than 50 engineers, professors, and students from the Seoul area attended a DVD replay of the ISSCC 2007 short courses at Korea University on 7 December, 2007. The lectures presented the fundamental limitations of nanometer CMOS and state-of-the-art circuit and system-level techniques. At the same meeting, the chapter celebrated its 10th anniversary.

articleTitle: Asad Abidi Recognized for Work in RF-CMOS
abstract: Asad Abidi will be awarded the IEEE Donald O. Pederson Award in Solid-State Circuits in February 2008 at the ISSCC Plenary "for pioneering and sustained contributions in the development of RF-CMOS."

articleTitle: SSCS-Green Mountain Organizes 17th IEEE North Atlantic Test Workshop, IEEE NATW Special Session on Solid-State Circuits & System Test Held on 14–16 May, 2008
abstract: Sponsored by the SSCS-Green Mountain chapter on May 14-16, 2008, the 17th annual North Atlantic Test Workshop (NATV) included a special session on solid-state circuits and system test focused on advances in built-in self-test for 65nm and 45nm nodes, adaptive test, and on-product reliability testing. Featured presenters were IBM's Mike Ouellette, Matt Grady and Kevin Stawiasz.

articleTitle: CEDA Currents, EDA Research Vital to Continued Industry Growth
abstract: EDA Research Vital to Continued Industry Growth    For the past 25 years, EDA has moved from systems houses to a new commercially viable industry; but research has centered in academia, where the link to a commercial endeavor is not as tight or as seamless as it is within the semiconductor industry. For EDA to support future design requirements, the current way of doing business must change. Research and industry continuity is a goal of CEDA's yearly Design Autmation Conference (DAC).

articleTitle: Leuven Student Branch and SSCS Chapters Organize 2nd SSCS-Benelux Microelectronics Symposium
abstract: The second annual Microelectronics Symposium at K.U.Leuven, organized by the IEEE-Leuven Student Branch and SSCS-Benelux chapters in March, 2008 with the help of On Semiconductor (formerly AMIS) and NXP, featured five invited talks on how industry and research institutions cope with constraints such as cost, energy consumption, and silicon area to advance the current state-of-the-art.

articleTitle: SSCS AdCom Endorses Newsletter-Magazine Conversion in Summer Meeting, ISSCC Task Force Previews Ground-Breaking Initiatives
abstract: ISSCC Task Force Previews Ground-Breaking InitiativesIn a formal motion at its biannual meeting on 19 August, 2008 in San Francisco, the SSCS AdCom endorsed the tone, scope, administrative structure, and budget of the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Magazine approved by the IEEE Technical Activities Board (TAB) in June. The Magazine will launch in January 2009 as an official migration of the SSCS Newsletter, which had become a magazine. The AdCom also heard about work in progress report on ISSCC spin-off "satellite" conferences and the ground-breaking technologies that will be necessary to support them.

articleTitle: Letters to the Editor
abstract: Letters are from retired analog designer Byron Blanchard, Larry Dobbins of The Franklin Institute, Bruce Tesch (Senior Technical Staff, Maxim Integrated Products) and Sven E. Wahlstrom and Richard Foss commenting on Dr. Foss's essay in the Winter 2008 issue of the News

articleTitle: Van der Spiegel Acclaimed for Educational Innovation at IEEE EAB Meeting
abstract: SSCS Chapters Chair Jan Van der Spiegel received the IEEE 2007 EAB Major Educational Innovation Award at the IEEE Educational Activities Board Awards Dinner in Boston, MA on 16 November, 2007 "for his efforts in promoting undergraduate research and creating robust opportunities for undergraduate students to enrich their education through integrative research experiences."

articleTitle: Sansen and Matsuzawa Visit National Taiwan University, Meeting and Seminars in April Organized by SSCS-Taipei Chapter
abstract: SSCS President Willy Sansen and AdCom member Akira Matsuzawa met with National Taiwan University President Prof. Si-Chen on 24 April, 2008. In a lecture there, Sansen termed the continuing advancement of microelectronics technologies "More Moore," and labeled the emerging trend toward integrated sensor and MEMS applications "More Than Moore." Prof. Matsuzawa spoke on the history and future of high-speed ADC's.

articleTitle: IEEE SSCS Joint Chapter Formed in Penang, Malaysia
abstract: Founded in 2005, Penang's MTT/ED/AP chapter was reorganized officially in May to better focus on related industries in the Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone in Malaysia and renamed the IEEE Microwave Theory and Techniques Society, the IEEE Electron Devices Society and the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Society (MTT/ED/SSC)joint chapter

articleTitle: SSCS Distinguished Lecturers Visit Athens and Varna
abstract: The Society's Region 8 DL Tour, hosted by Athanassios Skodras (SSCS-Greece) and Jordan Kolev (SSCS-Varna) in September 2007, included Ian Galton, John Long, Mircea Stan and Takayasu Sakurai. Remote attendees in Greece were able to pose questions via email or skype to the Chapter Chair.

articleTitle: Nine Lecturers Join SSCS DL Program, Roster Totals 30 Speakers
abstract: Roster Totals 30 Speakers The Society's Distinguished Lecturer Program is pleased to announce the election of 14 Distinguished Lecturers for 2008-2009, welcoming nine new speakers and five carried over from the previous term. According to DL Program Chair C. K. Ken Yang, the incoming group will enhance the program's coverage of RF and Analog, sensors, memories, and technology directions. Local chapters are encouraged to take advantage of this expertise.

articleTitle: CEDA Currents
abstract: Since its founding in 2005, the Council on Electronic Design Automation has sponsored an impressive list of publications, conferences, workshops, and new activities focused on advancing the EDA profession. Today, CEDA is a financially sound, permanent council of the IEEE thanks to Al Dunlop, its creator and first president, its officers and committee chairs. Newly elected Executive Committee members are John Darringer (President), Andreas Kuehlmann, (President-Elect), Al Dunlop (Past President and Nominations Committee Chair), Soha Hassoun (Vice President of Activities), Bill Joyner (Vice President of Conferences and acting Awards Committee Chair), Donatella Sciuto (Vice President of Finance), Rajesh Gupta (Vice President of Publications) and David Atienza (Secretary).

articleTitle: Editor's Column
abstract: This final issue of the SSCS News features an extensive new article by Gordon Bell entitled "Bell's Law for the Birth and Death of Computer Classes: A Theory of the Computer's Evolution." We also print two additional articles on the influence of Dr. Eric Vittoz by Joyce Kwong and Anantha Chandrakasan of MIT and by Dr. Erik H. M. Heijne of CERN, plus a classic paper written in 1981 by Dr.Vittoz, who was the Feature Author of our Summer '08 issue.

articleTitle: ISSCC 2008 Plenary Talks Spotlight Futuristic Consumer Electronics, Buxton and Muller Presentations Recapped and Illustrated
abstract: Buxton and Muller Presentations Recapped and Illustrated Bill Buxton discussed "surface computing" -- large flat touch-sensitive displays mounted on a wall or used as interactive tables that will be integrated into our work and living environments much like furniture or art. New developments in large inexpensive display technologies empower this emerging type of computational device. Mike Muller commented on the challenges facing embedded processor designers as technology penetrates every day life. Electronic devices empowered by embedded processor cores require partnerships among core developers, semiconductor companies, and OEMs, and demand close attention to technology trends, from fundamental technology to application requirements.

articleTitle: SSCS-Germany Cosponsors SAMOS 2007
abstract: Conference Founder Stamatis Vassiliadis Memorialized Conference founder Prof. Stamatis Vassiliadis, who passed away on 7 April, 2007 was memorialized at the 2007 SAMOS VII meeting on the Greek island of Samos from 16-19 July. SAMOS's organizing committee established the "Stamatis Vassiliadis Best Paper Awards" program to perpetuate his inspiration.

articleTitle: 230 Papers Represent International Community at ASICON 2007 in Guilin, China
abstract: 7th International ASIC Conference Organized by SSCS-Shanghai and Fudan University SSCS-Shanghai and Fudan University jointly organized the 7th International ASIC Conference (ASICON), which took place on 26-29 October, 2007 in Guilin, China. Held seven times since 1994 and sponsored by IEEE, the Institution of Engineering & Technology (IET), and the Chinese Institute of Electronics (CIE), the conference provides a forum for researchers, students, and engineers working in the fields of SOC/VLSI circuit design.

articleTitle: Classic Books and New Releases Share Best-Seller Status at ISSCC 2008, Niknejad's “Electromagnetics for High-Speed Analog and Digital Communication Circuits” and Books by Best, Pan-Samaddar and Maloberti are “Two-Year Phenomena”
abstract: Niknejad's "Electromagnetics for High-Speed Analog and Digital Communication Circuits" and Books by Best, Pan-Samaddar and Maloberti are Two-Year Phenomena An instant attraction that sold out immediately in 2007, "Electromagnetics for High-Speed Analog and Digital Communication Circuits," by Ali M. Niknejad remained the top conference seller in 2008. "Phase Locked Loops 6/e," by Roland E. Best, "Charge Pump Circuit Design," by Feng Pan and Tapan Samaddar, "Data Converters," by Franco Maloberti and "Nonvolatile Memory Technologies," edited by Joe Brewer and Manzur Gill also sold best for a second year. Top new titles were "Switch Mode Power Supplies," by Christophe P. Basso, "mm-Wave Silicon Technology-60 GHz and Beyond," edited by Ali M. Niknejad and Hossein Hashemi, and "Memory Systems - Cache, DRAM, Disk," by B. Jacob, S. Ng and D. Wang. Enduring best sellers were "Analog Design Essentials," by Willy Sansen and "CMOS: Circuit Design, Layout, and Simulation, 2nd Edition," by R. Jacob Baker.

articleTitle: Solid-State Circuits Magazine and Redesigned Website to Launch in 2009
abstract: The print Solid-State Circuits Magazine, hosted also on IEEE Xplore, will exceed the format of the SSCS Newsletter with enriched educational material, tutorials, special interest pieces, bibliographies, and distillations of cutting-edge work from scholarly publications and technical conference papers. The Society's new website will include scrollable windows listing the contents of the current JSSC and Magazine plus a comprehensive list of SSCS-sponsored meetings, breaking news about chapters and distinguished lectures, and IEEE conference and field awards, plus IEEE member programs like Expert Now and IEEE.tv. The SSCS membership email blast will continue to announce important upcoming conferences, deadlines, and member activities on a schedule that will maximize their timeliness

articleTitle: IEEE DL Vojin Oklobdzija Visits Istanbul in May, focuses on low power digital design in talks at two universities
abstract: Focuses on Low Power Digital Design in DL Talks at Two Universities IEEE Distinguished Lecturer Prof. Vojin Oklobdzija delivered two talks on low power digital design on 29 May, 2008 at Istanbul Technical University (ITU) and at Bogazici University (BU), also in Istanbul. He focused on the problem of increasing power consumption by high-complexity digital integrated circuits, prospects for the future, how power efficiency can be defined, the effect of parameters such as power supply and device size on power efficiency, and design suggestions to reduce power consumption.

articleTitle: New recruit to the SSCS editorial team
abstract: The author introdices himself as the Chief Executive of the Institute for System Level Integration (ISLI) in Edinburgh, Scotland who has joined the SSCS News as Associate Editor for Europe/Africa. His plans for articles throughout the coming year are report. they include topics such as the drive for cost-effective development, the quest for competitive margins, the need to maintain innovation and associated challenges such as the geographical dispersion of development resources, new and emerging players, and key driving technologies, as well as an exploration of vital areas for a successful symbiotic relationship between academia and industry.

articleTitle: New York EDS/SSCS IEEE Chapter Formed in October 2007, Aims to Link Academics and Industrial Researchers in the NY Metropolitan Area
abstract: Aims to Link Academics and Industrial Researchers in the NY Metropolitan Area. Because IEEE's New York section covers the five boroughs of New York City and Westchester and Rockland counties, the chapter plans to hold half its meetings in Westchester and half in New York City. Initial chapter activities will focus on a series of seminars with overlapping appeal to the local SSCS and ED community that will complement technical events held by other societies and IEEE units in the New York metropolitan area.

articleTitle: ISSCC Student Forum 2009
abstract: A Networking Venue and Communications Challenge The ISSCC Student Forum will return to the Society's flagship conference on Sunday afternoon, 8 February 2009 with presentations extending into the evening for the first time. The Student Forum provides a networking opportunity for M.S. and Ph.D. candidates at an early stage in their post-undergraduate schooling and offers them practice in the hi-tech communications challenge -- the five-minute presentation

articleTitle: Now It's Japan's Turn to Host, 4th Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference, November 3–5, 2008, Fukuoka, Japan
abstract: 4th Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference, November 3-5, 2008, Fukuoka, Japan The fourth A-SSCC will be held on 3-5 November in Fukuoka, Japan. Its unique Industry Program will examine the IC industry dynamics that have resulted in a blossoming semiconductor business in Asia by spotlighting state-of-the-art technological achievements, emerging product chips, and the speed at which research results are turned to actual products. A-SSCC is fully sponsored by the IEEE Solid-State Circuits Society

articleTitle: The International Conference on Computer Aided Design (ICCAD) Previews Novel Program, External Workshops will Collocate with ICCAD on 10–13 November in San Jose
abstract: External Workshops will Collocate with International Conference on Computer Aided Design on 10-13 November , 2008 in San Jose The International Conference on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD) 2008 will offer 122 outstanding papers split into 40 sessions over three days in San Jose from 10-13 November, plus four half-day tutorials, three embedded tutorials, and two special designer sessions providing additional perspectives. ICCAD will also open its doors to new external workshops which will be collocated with the conference.

articleTitle: Custom Integrated Circuits Conference (CICC) Celebrates 30th Year, More than 400 Expected on 21-24 September in San Jose
abstract: More than 400 Expected on 21-24 September in San Jose More than 400 engineers are expected to attend the 30th CICC in San Diego, CA on 21-24 September. The conference, which is fully sponsored by SSCS, will consider the latest trends and circuit techniques for analog and digital ICs, major university and industrial research on ADCs, PLLs, RF-circuits, high-speed transceivers, and 3D integration, and how circuit designers are solving major issues today on power, variation, noise, jitter, GHz performance, system-on-chip integration, and limits to CMOS scaling.

articleTitle: 2008 IEEE Compound Semiconductor IC Symposium (CSICS) to Collocate with BCTM in October
abstract: The 2008 CSIC Symposium, collocated with BCTM on 12-15 October in Monterey, CA will offer its annual Primer Course on Basics of Compound Semiconductor ICs, a three-day technical program with approximately 60 papers and four panels, two short courses on phased arrays and RF, and a vendor exhibition.

articleTitle: 2008 IEEE BIPOLAR/BICMOS Circuits and Technology Conference (BCTM) to Meet in Monterey in October
abstract: Everyone interested in cutting-edge processes, devices, and circuits used in state-of-the-art telecommunications and power control systems will not want to miss BCTM on October 13-15 in Monterey, CA. Focusing especially on HBT BiCMOS, BCTM will include a one-day short course, two full days of invited and contributed papers and a keynote address by Dr. Gil Amelio, CEO of Jazz Semiconductor, entitled, "Technology Cnvergency Creating new Opportunities for Innovation."

articleTitle: Preview of EDSSC2008 in Hong Kong, Three-day Program in December to Feature 150 Papers and Plenary Talks by SSCS DLs T. Kawahara and I. Young
abstract: Three-Day Program in December to Feature 150 Papers and Plenary Talks by SSCS DLs T. Kawahara and I. Young The 4th IEEE International Conference on Electron Devices and Solid-State Circuits (EDSSC2008) will be a three-day program from 8-10 December, 2008 featuring 150 technical papers covering broad areas in electron devices and solid-state circuits. The event is being organized by the IEEE Electron Devices/Solid-State Circuits Hong Kong Joint Chapter, and sponsored by the Hong Kong Applied Science and Technology Institute and K. C. Wong Education Foundation.

articleTitle: SSCS Events Calendar
abstract: Provides a listing of upcoming events of interest to practitioners and researchers.

articleTitle: Call for Nominations for Sensors Awards, Deadline for three awards is August 15
abstract: SSCS is a founding member of the Sensors Council, which recognizes individuals who are recommended by its Societies. Please take the initiative to nominate candidiates for the Council's Technical Achievement Award, Meritorious Service Award, and Journal Best Paper Award by 15 August, 2008.

articleTitle: IEEE Solid-State Circuit Society News - Cover
abstract: Presents the table of contents for this issue of the periodical.

articleTitle: Invitation from the ISSCC 2008 Technical Program Chair
abstract: The conference theme is "System Integration for Life and Style" in recognition that integration of novel circuits and systems can deliver functions that enrich the users' life style. There will be 237 papers distributed over 31 technical sessions covering advances in analog and digital circuits; data converters; imagers, medical and displays; MEMS; memories; RF building blocks; technology directions, and wireless and wireline communications.

articleTitle: IEEE Solid-State Circuit Society News - Table of contents
abstract: Presents the table of contents for this issue of the periodical.

articleTitle: IEEE Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits Symposium (RFIC) to Open Microwave Week 2008 in Atlanta
abstract: The IEEE Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits (RFIC) Symposium will return to Atlanta, Georgia on 15-17 June 2008, adding to the excitement of Microwave Week with three days focused exclusively on RFIC technology and innovation. An Interactive Forum, two panel sessions covering nearly all facets of RFIC technology, and 27 paper sessions will be given on Monday and Tuesday, 16-17 June. On Sunday, June 15th, the symposium will offer 12 workshops and tutorials and a plenary session in the evening with two keynote addresses given by renowned industry leaders.

articleTitle: ISLPED Moves to Asia in 2008, International Symposium on Low Power Electronics to Meet in Bangalore on 11–13 August
abstract: International Symposium on Low Power Electronics to Meet in Bangalore on 11-13 August ISLPED will take place in Bangalore -- India's Silicon Valley -- on the campus of one of the country's premier graduate schools, the Indian Institute of Science. The program, comprised of two concurrent tracks on circuit and system aspects, will offer a unique opportunity for identifying synergies between circuit, system, and application designers in meeting power budgets.

articleTitle: ISSCC 2009 Feb 8–12 Preview
abstract: Focusing in 2009 on Adaptive Circuits and Systems, ISSCC will offer four plenary talks, approximately 250 technical papers, nine evening panels and special evening sessions, all included in the registration price. Information about these events and the eight ISSCC 2009 circuit design forums, ten 90-minute tutorials, and an all-day Short Course on "Low-Voltage Analog and Mixed-Signal CMOS Circuit Design" will be published on the conference website in November.

articleTitle: ICUWB 2009 to Focus on Microvave and Millimeter Wave Band Technology, IEEE International Conference on Ultra-Wideband will Meet on 9–11 September 2009 in Vancouver
abstract: IEEE International Conference on Ultra-Wideband Will Meet on 9 - 11 September 2009 in Vancouver In Vancouver on 9-11 September, the 2009 IEEE International Conference on Ultra-Wideband will center around the topic of UWB transmission in micro-wave and millimeter wave bands and over power lines. It will focus on the latest advances in UWB technology, current and future applications ranging from UWB communication for personal area and sensor networks to UWB-based localization and positioning systems to UWB vehicular radar and imaging systems, and standardization and regulation for UWB transmission

articleTitle: 2007 VLSI-TSA/DAT Best Paper Awards Presented in Hsinchu, April, 2008
abstract: In opening ceremonies on 21 and 23 April, 2008, the 2008 International Symposia on VLSI Technology, Systems and Applications (VLSI-TSA) and VLSI Design, Automation and Test (VLSI-DAT) presented a Best Student Paper Award for 2007 to Donovan Lee, a graduate student at UC Berkeley, and a Best Presentation Award for 2007 to Prof. Tsung-Hsien Lin of National Taiwan University. SSCS is a cosponsor of both meetings.

articleTitle: 4th Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference – Digital Convergence for a Ubiquitous Lifestyle, More than 100 Papers Selected for Meeting on 3 – 5 November, Fukuoka, Japan
abstract: More than 100 Papers Selected for Meeting on 3 - 5 November, Fukuoka, Japan Travelling around major Asian countries such as Taiwan (2005), China (2006), and Korea (2007), the fourth Asian Solid-State Circuits Conference will take place in Japan from 3-5 November. It will offer three plenary talks and 116 papers representing 26 countries, four tutorial sessions, two panels, and its unique industrial program and acclaimed student design contest.

articleTitle: Hot Chips 20: Three Days of the Very Best in Highperformance Chips and Technologies, At Stanford University, 24–26 August, 2008
abstract: The 20th annual Hot Chips conference at Stanford University's Memorial Auditorium on August 24-26, 2008 will offer a tutorial on the challenges of solving the "memory wall" and a plenary address by Standford's Sebastian Thrun on "Cars that Drive Themselves." A second keynote by Dr. Richard Swanson will relate the history and technology of SunPower, a leading solar energy company.

articleTitle: Sister Conferences ESSCIRC/ESSDERC Meet on 15–19 September, The 2008 European Forum for Solid-State Circuits is in Edinburgh, Scotland
abstract: 2008 European Forum for Solid-State Circuits is in Edinburgh, Scotland   This year's ESSCIRC/ESSDERC conferences on 15-19 September at the Edinburgh International Conference Centre (EICC) will share six keynote presentations and technical sessions on topics bridging both communities while keeping separate Technical Programs. In adddition to six workshops, ESSCIRC tutorials will cover CMOS at the "bleeding edge," nanoelectronics, and integrating CMOS with other technologies.

articleTitle: Abidi Receives IEEE Pederson Award at ISSCC 2008
abstract: SSCS President Willy Sansen presented the IEEE Donald O. Pederson Award in Solid-State Circuits to Asad A. Abidi at the ISSCC Plenary Session on 4 February. Quoting an evaluator, he lauded Dr. Abidi as "someone who has insight into technical problems that baffle others -- a visionary who often heralds activities in totally new research areas."

articleTitle: JSSC 2006 Best Paper Award Presented to J.B. Ashbrook, H.-M. Bae, S. Chopra, J. Park, N.R. Shanbhag and A.C. Singer
abstract: "This paper heralds a new era in the design of integrated circuits by demonstrating the feasibility of implementing sophisticated communication techniques employed in wireless and other wireline channels at optical line rates. Such techniques are critical for the future deployment of 40 Gb/s and 100 Gb/s links and thus represent a new opportunity for circuit designers." K. Nagaraj, JSSC Editor, 2007

articleTitle: ISSCC 2008 to Focus on System Integration for Life and Style, SSCS Flagship Conference to Meet on February 3–7 in San Francisco
abstract: SSCS Flagship Conference to Meet on February 3-7 in San Francisco ISSCC 2008 will feature presentations that demonstrate ways in which the integration of novel circuit and systems can deliver functions that enrich the users' life style. Following the Plenary Session with addresses by four speakers, 237 technical papers will be presented in 31 sessions over 2 1/2 days, highlighting the latest advancements in circuit design.

articleTitle: VLSI-TSA and VLSI-DAT to Convene on 21–25 April in Hsinchu, Taiwan, 15th International Symposium on VLSI Technology, Systems, and Applications & 4th VLSI Design, Automation and Test
abstract: 15th International Symposium on VLSI Technology, Systems, and Applications & 4th VLSI Design, Automation and Test Divided into two separate annual symposia since 2005, VLSI TSA-DAT lasts for two and a half days in the same week, with a one day overlap. In 2008 each symposium will feature three keynote speakers. The aim of the joint conference is to bring together scientists and engineers actively engaged in research, development, and manufacturing on VLSI technology, systems, and applications and on VLSI design, automation and test to discuss current progress in this field.

articleTitle: 2008 Symposium on VLSI Circuits in Honolulu on 18–20 June
abstract: For the first time this year, the Symposium on VLSI Circuits will overlap the VLSI Technology Symposium by two full days. This schedule will allow registrants attending papers from either symposium to learn about the latest advances in VLSI circuits and technology and to exchange ideas with people from both meetings.

articleTitle: 18th VLSI Design/CAD Symposium Cosponsored by IEEE Taipei and Tainan Sections
abstract: Annual Meeting of IEEE SSCS and CAS in August The 18th VLSI/CAD Symposium was held on 8-10 August, 2007 in Hualien, Taiwan. Cosponsored this year by SSCS-Taipei and SSCS-Tainan, the meeting plays an important role in stimulating local research in Taiwan, which is home to prominent semiconductor foundries and renowned as an IC design power house.

articleTitle: SSCS-Montreal Receives Outstanding Chapter Award for 2007
abstract: Founded in 1999, SSCS-Montreal includes over forty SSCS members and hundreds of students, and spans several industrial companies and universities. The co-sponsorship of Montreal chapter activities by the Microsystems Research Alliance of Quebec (ReSMiQ) has been key in enabling the organization to enjoy a broad range of activities. According to the Chapter's co-chairs, the key for managing an effective SSCS Chapter is to create and sustain enthusiasm for custom solid-state circuits through serving the learning needs of current Chapter members and attracting new members, especially students.

articleTitle: Chandrakasan Discusses Micro-power Integrated Circuits and Systems in Ottawa, SSCS Chapter Hosts DL Talk at Carleton University in December
abstract: SSCS-Ottawa Hosts DL Talk at Carleton University in December In a talk in Ottawa, MIT's Anantha Chandrakasan said the design of micro-power systems will enable operation using energy scavenging. The opportunities and challenges associated with sub-threshold design include variation-aware design for logic and SRAM circuits, efficient DC-DC converters for ultra-low-voltage delivery, and algorithm structuring to support extreme parallelism, he said.
